metadata.title: feat(security): add custom Semgrep rules for MCP patterns (#2237)
metadata.author: Arnav08Sanghi

description:
**Issue**  
#2217  

📝 **Summary**  
This PR adds MCP-specific Semgrep rules to the Source Scanner plugin to improve detection of critical and best-practice security issues in MCP server code. It also includes response validation rules to catch unsafe or sensitive data being returned from tools.  

**Update/Fixes**  
- Added new Semgrep rulesets: `mcp-security-critical`, `mcp-security-best-practices`, `mcp-response-security`.  
- Each ruleset includes Python-specific patterns for:  
  - **Command injection** (`os.system`, `subprocess`)  
  - **SQL injection** (unparameterized queries)  
  - **Path traversal & arbitrary file access**  
  - **SSRF** (unvalidated URLs)  
  - **Deserialization & response injection**  
  - **Credential exposure & hardcoded secrets**  
  - **Input validation, DoS prevention, maintainability checks**  
  - **Response output validation and exception handling**  
- Updated existing Semgrep runner to integrate the new rulesets.  
- Minor fixes: logging instead of `print()`, copyright headers updated to 2026.  

**New Functionality**  
- Source Scanner now uses MCP-specific rules to detect security issues that are **critical**, **best-practice violations**, or **response/output risks**.  
- Rules are packaged so they can be extended with additional MCP server-specific patterns in the future.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The f-string pattern `os.system(f"...{$ARG}...")` uses `...` inside the string literal, but Semgrep’s `...` wildcard doesn’t apply inside Python string literals. This will only match code that literally contains three dots, so it will miss typical `os.system(f"{user_input}")` style cases. Consider matching `os.system(f$S)` and then constraining `$S` (e.g., via `metavariable-regex` / `pattern-regex`) instead of embedding `...` in the string.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
These SQL-injection patterns use `...` inside string literals (e.g., `"SELECT ... {$ARG} ..."`), which makes `...` literal text rather than a Semgrep wildcard. As written, the rule will not match real-world dynamic SQL construction (f-strings, `%` formatting, concatenation). A more reliable approach is to match `cursor.execute($Q)` / `db.query($Q)` and then use metavariable constraints to detect formatting/concatenation with untrusted input, or use `pattern-regex` on the query expression.
```suggestion
          - pattern: cursor.execute($Q)
          - pattern: db.execute($Q)
          - pattern: db.query($Q)
      - metavariable-pattern:
          metavariable: $Q
          patterns:
            - pattern-either:
                - pattern: f"...{$ARG}..."
                - pattern: "..." + $ARG
                - pattern: $ARG + "..."
                - pattern: "..." % $ARG
                - pattern: "..." % ($ARG, ...)
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
The hardcoded-secret patterns are currently matching literal placeholder strings like `"sk_..."` and `"......"`, which is unlikely to detect real secrets and may create a false sense of coverage. Consider using `metavariable-regex`/`pattern-regex` to match common secret formats (and keep the regex conservative to avoid noisy false positives).
```suggestion
          - pattern-regex: (?i)\bapi_key\s*=\s*["']sk_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}["']
          - pattern-regex: (?i)\bpassword\s*=\s*["'][^"'\\s]{8,}["']
          - pattern-regex: (?i)\bAPIKEY\s*=\s*["'][A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}["']
          - pattern-regex: (?i)\bSECRET_KEY\s*=\s*["'][A-Za-z0-9_./+=-]{20,}["']
          - pattern-regex: (?i)\btoken\s*=\s*["']Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{16,}["']
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
`return {"text": ...$DATA...}` is not valid Python syntax (there’s no operator between the ellipsis and `$DATA`), and is likely to be rejected by Semgrep’s parser. If the intent is to catch returning external content derived from `$DATA`, match the value as an expression metavariable (e.g., `return {"text": $T}`) and constrain `$T` to include `$DATA` via `pattern`/`metavariable-pattern` rather than attempting `...$DATA...`.
```suggestion
                  return {"text": $TEXT}
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $TEXT
                  pattern-either:
                    - pattern: $DATA
                    - pattern: $DATA.text
                    - pattern: f"...{$DATA}..."
                    - pattern: f"...{$DATA.text}..."
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
These patterns embed `...` inside Python f-strings (e.g., `logger.debug(f"...{args['api_key']}...")`). `...` will be treated as literal characters inside the string, so the rule won’t match typical log statements. Prefer matching the call shape (e.g., `logger.$LVL(f$S)` / `print(f$S)`) and then constraining `$S` to reference the sensitive argument via metavariable matching.
```suggestion
          - patterns:
              - pattern: logger.debug(f$S)
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $S
                  pattern: "{...{args['api_key']}...}"
          - patterns:
              - pattern: logger.info(f$S)
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $S
                  pattern: "{...{args['password']}...}"
          - patterns:
              - pattern: print(f$S)
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $S
                  pattern: "{...{args['token']}...}"
          - patterns:
              - pattern: logger.error(f$S)
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $S
                  pattern: "{...{args['secret']}...}"
          - patterns:
              - pattern: logger.warning(f$S)
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $S
                  pattern: "{...{arguments['bearer']}...}"
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
`return TextContent(text=f"...{{...}}...")` likely doesn’t do what’s intended: `{{`/`}}` in Python f-strings escapes literal braces, so this matches literal `{`/`}` characters rather than interpolation of unescaped content. If the goal is to detect returning interpolated/markup-like content, match `TextContent(text=f$S)` and then constrain `$S` (or match specific dangerous literals/constructs) rather than relying on `...{{...}}...`.
```suggestion
          - pattern: return TextContent(text=f$S)
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
Rule name/message indicate it detects *missing* try/except, but the patterns currently match any `requests.get/open/cursor.execute/urlopen` inside a function regardless of whether it’s already wrapped in a try/except. This will produce many false positives. Consider adding a `pattern-not-inside: try: ... except ...:` (or equivalent) so it only flags I/O that is not already guarded.
```suggestion
              ...
      - pattern-not-inside: |
          try:
              ...
          except ...:
              ...
```

comments.author: Copilot
Copilot
Copilot
comments.body:
These patterns include `...` inside f-strings, which will be treated as literal characters and will miss most real code. To detect “user-provided URL used in request”, match the call shape (e.g., `requests.get($URL)` / `urlopen($URL)`) and then constrain `$URL` to be derived from `args[...]` rather than trying to approximate with `f"...{...}..."`.
```suggestion
          - pattern: requests.get($URL)
          - pattern: urllib.request.urlopen($URL)
      - metavariable-pattern:
          metavariable: $URL
          pattern-either:
            - pattern: args[$KEY]
            - pattern: arguments[$KEY]
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
Like the response ruleset, this “missing error handling” rule currently matches I/O calls in any function, even when they are already inside a try/except. This will generate a lot of noise. Add a `pattern-not-inside: try: ... except ...:` (or similar) so it only flags unguarded external calls.
```suggestion
              ...
      - pattern-not-inside: |
          try:
              ...
          except ...:
              ...
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: These rule files are described as being “used by the source scanner”, but in the current repo there doesn’t appear to be any source-scanner integration and the existing `make semgrep` target runs `uvx semgrep --config=auto` (no reference to `semgrep-rules/mcp/*`). Unless there’s another runner not included in this PR, these rules may never execute. Consider wiring these configs into the Semgrep invocation (e.g., adding `--config semgrep-rules/mcp/mcp-security-critical.yaml` etc., or a top-level aggregate config) and/or updating docs to reflect the actual integration point.
